You are helping a member-governed AI cooperative make sense of an anonymous braindump survey before a members' meeting. You will receive a batch of survey responses. Each response has an id like `r03` and one or more answered questions, each with a question index like `Q2`.

Extract every distinct, atomic point a respondent makes. One point per item. Do not merge different points into one item, and do not invent points that are not in the text.

For each item return:

- `id`: the response id it came from (e.g. `r03`).
- `q`: the question index it came from (e.g. `Q2`).
- `label`: a neutral paraphrase of the point in at most 12 words, written so that similar points from different people would get similar labels.
- `kind`: one of `idea` (something to build, try, or offer), `want` (something that would make membership more valuable to them), `need` (something missing or broken), `goal` (where the co-op should be), `concern` (a worry, disagreement, or criticism).
- `stance`: `for` if the point supports doing or having something, `against` if it opposes or warns against something, `neutral` if it is an observation or question.
- `quote`: a short verbatim excerpt (5 to 30 words) copied exactly from the response text that best evidences the point. It must be a character-for-character substring of the source text. Do not paraphrase, do not fix typos, do not add ellipses.

Skip pleasantries, empty answers, and "nothing to add". Keep the respondent's framing; do not editorialize.

Return exactly one fenced ```json block and nothing else, shaped as:

```json
{"items": [{"id": "r03", "q": "Q2", "label": "...", "kind": "idea", "stance": "for", "quote": "..."}]}
```

## Response r01

### r01 / Q1: What drew you to the co-op, and what do you use it for today?
Privacy. I wanted an AI I could use for client work without feeding a big vendor. Mostly chat, some API from scripts.

### r01 / Q2: Ideas. What should the co-op build, try, or offer next?
A shared prompt library members can contribute to. Also a Matrix bot that answers questions about the docs.

### r01 / Q3: Wants. What would make membership more valuable to you personally?
A cheaper tier for light users; I barely touch my allowance most months.

### r01 / Q4: Needs. What is missing, broken, or in your way right now?
The chat loses my place on mobile when I switch apps. Also the model picker names are confusing (dotted vs dashed slugs).

### r01 / Q5: Goals. Where should the co-op be a year from now?
Fifty members, real elections, and at least one model we host ourselves.

### r01 / Q6: Dissent. What worries you, what do you disagree with, or what are we getting wrong?
I worry we are spreading across too many providers. Three providers is already hard to explain to a new member.

## Response r02

### r02 / Q1: What drew you to the co-op, and what do you use it for today?
Green energy mostly. I teach and wanted something I could recommend to students with a straight face.

### r02 / Q2: Ideas. What should the co-op build, try, or offer next?
Classroom or group accounts: one payment, several seats, shared budget.

### r02 / Q3: Wants. What would make membership more valuable to you personally?
Being able to see the energy and emissions per conversation, not just tokens.

### r02 / Q4: Needs. What is missing, broken, or in your way right now?
Onboarding email landed in spam for two of my students. The email-must-match rule tripped one of them.

### r02 / Q5: Goals. Where should the co-op be a year from now?
A recognized option for universities and nonprofits, with an institutional tier.

### r02 / Q6: Dissent. What worries you, what do you disagree with, or what are we getting wrong?
Not dissent exactly, but the Loomio threads are long and I cannot keep up.

### r02 / Q7: Anything else?
Thank you for doing this.

## Response r03

### r03 / Q1: What drew you to the co-op, and what do you use it for today?
Curiosity about co-op governance. I use the API from a small writing tool I maintain.

### r03 / Q2: Ideas. What should the co-op build, try, or offer next?
An institutional or app-partner membership so projects like mine can buy inference for their users through the co-op instead of each user joining separately.

### r03 / Q3: Wants. What would make membership more valuable to you personally?
Stable model names. When tinfoil/glm-5-3-flash disappeared my app broke.

### r03 / Q4: Needs. What is missing, broken, or in your way right now?
No deprecation notice period for models. No status page.

### r03 / Q5: Goals. Where should the co-op be a year from now?
A documented SLA-ish commitment, even an informal one, and a changelog members can subscribe to.

### r03 / Q6: Dissent. What worries you, what do you disagree with, or what are we getting wrong?
I think the terms forbidding any redistribution of access will block exactly the kind of mission-aligned projects we say we want.

## Response r04

### r04 / Q1: What drew you to the co-op, and what do you use it for today?
A friend invited me. I mostly use the chat for drafting emails.

### r04 / Q2: Ideas. What should the co-op build, try, or offer next?
Voice mode on the phone app.

### r04 / Q3: Wants. What would make membership more valuable to you personally?
Honestly it is fine as is.

### r04 / Q5: Goals. Where should the co-op be a year from now?
More members so it keeps existing.

## Response r05

### r05 / Q1: What drew you to the co-op, and what do you use it for today?
Wanted to support a cooperative alternative. I use it daily for coding help.

### r05 / Q2: Ideas. What should the co-op build, try, or offer next?
Self-host at least one open model on our own hardware so we are not just reselling other people's APIs.

### r05 / Q3: Wants. What would make membership more valuable to you personally?
Higher allowance for people who pay more; the flat $15 cap makes paying extra feel pointless.

### r05 / Q4: Needs. What is missing, broken, or in your way right now?
Tool calling is flaky on some models and there is no doc saying which ones support it.

### r05 / Q5: Goals. Where should the co-op be a year from now?
Our own GPU box, even a small one, and a path to more.

### r05 / Q6: Dissent. What worries you, what do you disagree with, or what are we getting wrong?
Self-hosting will cost more than buying tokens and we should be honest about that before voting for it.

### r05 / Q7: Anything else?
Happy to help with ops.
